Types

Name Description

argon2_parameters

Argon2’s parameters (spec 2.15), defined in argon2.hpp; declared here for the engines.

argon2id_parameters

The costs of Argon2id with one lane, as libsodium’s crypto_pwhash takes them, for argon2id.

blake3

BLAKE3, its keyed mode, its key derivation and its extendable output, over the official C implementation, in Boost.Hash2’s HashAlgorithm form.

digest_options

The parameters of a digest (spec 2.15), defined in digest.hpp; declared here for the engines, which take them.

hasher

A hash fed in pieces, with one result: make, update as often as the data comes, then finish once (spec 2.15).

kbkdf_options

The fixed input of SP 800-108’s KBKDF in counter mode, defined in kdf_standards.hpp; declared here for the engines.

keccak_256

Keccak-256 with the original padding, Ethereum’s hash, in Boost.Hash2’s HashAlgorithm form.

mac_options

The parameters of a MAC (spec 2.15), defined in mac.hpp; declared here for the engines.

scrypt_parameters

The costs of scrypt, RFC 7914’s N, r and p.

Type Aliases

Name Description

default_async_backend

The backend of the asynchronous family when a call names none.

default_backend

The backend a function of Algorithm uses when the call names none (spec 4.1).

default_kdf_backend

The backend hkdf_extract, hkdf_expand, hkdf and pbkdf2 use when the program names none: default_backend of Kdf, backends::hash2 on every target.

digest

A digest of N bytes, Boost.Hash2’s.

hmac

HMAC over H, RFC 2104, Boost.Hash2’s.

Enums

Name Description

error

Why an operation of webcpp::hash failed.

Functions

Name Description

argon2

Argon2 version 0x13 (RFC 9106) of the variant Variant with every parameter: fills output from password and salt.

argon2id

Argon2id version 0x13 (RFC 9106) with one lane, no secret and no associated data: fills output_bytes from password_bytes and salt_bytes.

async_argon2

Argon2 of the variant Variant with every parameter (RFC 9106) on a thread of work’s context, as async_argon2id runs.

async_argon2id

Argon2id (RFC 9106, one lane) on a thread of work’s context (spec 11.5).

async_digest

Hashes input into output with the digest Digest, asynchronously (spec 11): on a synchronous backend, the default, at once, completing through a post on the handler’s associated executor (executor by default), never inside the call.

async_hkdf

HKDF (RFC 5869), extract and expand, asynchronously (spec 11), as async_digest runs: the output of hkdf<Hmac, Backend>.

async_hmac

The HMAC of input under key over the Boost.Hash2 hmac Hmac, asynchronously (spec 11), as async_digest runs: the tag of mac<macs::hmac<...>> over Hmac’s digest.

async_pbkdf2

PBKDF2 (RFC 8018), asynchronously.

async_scrypt

scrypt (RFC 7914) on a thread of work’s context, as async_argon2id runs.

blake2b_subkey

The subkey subkey_id of master_key in context, libsodium’s crypto_kdf_derive_from_key: keys for different purposes from one master key, each unrelated to the others and to the master key without it.

category

The category of every error.

digest_of

Hashes input into output with the digest Digest on Backend, in one call.

hkdf

HKDF (RFC 5869, section 2): extract, then expand.

hkdf_expand

HKDF-Expand (RFC 5869, section 2.3): fills output_bytes from prk_bytes and info_bytes.

hkdf_extract

HKDF-Extract (RFC 5869, section 2.2): the pseudorandom key of ikm_bytes under salt_bytes.

kbkdf

SP 800-108’s key-based key derivation (NIST SP 800-108r1, section 4.1, counter mode) over the HMAC Hmac: fills output from the key-derivation key key, each block an HMAC under key of the counter, then the fixed input options states.

mac

The tag of input under key, with the MAC Mac on Backend.

make_error_code

Makes the error_code of an error, as its implicit conversion does.

pbkdf2

PBKDF2 (RFC 8018, section 5.2): fills output_bytes from password_bytes and salt_bytes by iteration_count rounds of Hmac.

scrypt

scrypt (RFC 7914): fills output_bytes from password_bytes and salt_bytes.

sskdf

SP 800-56C’s one-step key derivation over the digest Digest (NIST SP 800-56C revision 2, section 4.1, with H a hash function): fills output from the shared secret secret and fixed_info, block after block, each Digest(counter || secret || fixed_info) with a 32-bit big-endian counter from 1.

x963kdf

ANSI X9.63’s key derivation (ANSI X9.63-2011, section 5.6.3; SEC 1 v2, section 3.6.1) over the digest Digest: fills output from the shared secret secret and shared_info, block after block, each Digest(secret || counter || shared_info) with a 32-bit big-endian counter from 1.

backend_has_v

backends::xkcp has digests::sha3_256 (XKCP’s FIPS 202’s Keccak_Hash).

backend_has_v

backends::xkcp has digests::sha3_384 (XKCP’s FIPS 202’s Keccak_Hash).

backend_has_v

backends::xkcp has digests::sha3_512 (XKCP’s FIPS 202’s Keccak_Hash).

backend_has_v

backends::xkcp has digests::shake_128 (XKCP’s FIPS 202’s Keccak_Hash, any output size).

backend_has_v

backends::xkcp has digests::shake_256 (XKCP’s FIPS 202’s Keccak_Hash, any output size).

backend_has_v

backends::xkcp has digests::tuplehash_128 (XKCP’s SP 800-185 TupleHash128, both forms).

backend_has_v

backends::xkcp has digests::tuplehash_256 (XKCP’s SP 800-185 TupleHash256, both forms).

backend_has_v

backends::xkcp has digests::turboshake_128 (XKCP’s TurboSHAKE, any output size and D).

backend_has_v

backends::xkcp has digests::turboshake_256 (XKCP’s TurboSHAKE, any output size and D).

backend_has_v

backends::bearssl has hkdf (not its two steps alone) over MD5, SHA-1 and four SHA-2s.

backend_has_v

backends::hash2 has HKDF over every Boost.Hash2 hmac whose result is a digest.

backend_has_v

backends::hash2 has PBKDF2 over every Boost.Hash2 hmac whose result is a digest.

backend_has_v

backends::openssl has HKDF over every alias of hmac.hpp but hmac_ripemd_128.

backend_has_v

backends::openssl has SP 800-108’s KBKDF in counter mode (OpenSSL 3.5.9’s EVP_KDF "KBKDF") over every alias of hmac.hpp but hmac_ripemd_128.

backend_has_v

backends::openssl has PBKDF2 over every alias of hmac.hpp but hmac_ripemd_128.

backend_has_v

HKDF-Expand alone: as HKDF-Extract, every backend with HKDF but backends::bearssl.

backend_has_v

HKDF-Extract alone: every backend that has HKDF over Hmac but backends::bearssl, whose br_hkdf_* keeps the pseudorandom key inside its context (spec 3.2).

blake2b_subkey_context_size

The size of blake2b_subkey’s context, in bytes (libsodium’s crypto_kdf_CONTEXTBYTES).

blake2b_subkey_key_size

The size of blake2b_subkey’s master key, in bytes (libsodium’s crypto_kdf_KEYBYTES).

blake2b_subkey_max_size

The longest subkey blake2b_subkey derives, in bytes (libsodium’s crypto_kdf_BYTES_MAX).

blake2b_subkey_min_size

The shortest subkey blake2b_subkey derives, in bytes (libsodium’s crypto_kdf_BYTES_MIN).

hkdf_max_info_size

The longest info every backend accepts, 32,768 bytes (OpenSSL 3.5’s limit).

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/hash/kdf.hpp>

    class Algorithm,
    class Hmac = void>
using default_backend = /* implementation-defined */::type;

Description

backends::hash2 for hkdf_extract, hkdf_expand, hkdf and pbkdf2, on every target and whatever the program links; backends::sodium for argon2id, scrypt (which backends::openssl also has, named in the call) and blake2b_subkey, which stops the build with the line to add to the Jamfile when the program does not link libsodium. A tag of the families defaults to the first of backends::hash2, backends::xkcp, backends::blake3 and backends::sodium that has it (design D34), or to detail::no_default, which refuses: the call names its backend. backends::bearssl and backends::openssl are never a default. No define changes it: another backend is chosen by naming it in the call, as `hkdf<hmac_sha2_256, backends::openssl>`.

webcpp::hash::blake3::blake3

Constructs a hash seeded by input_size bytes: plain when input_size is zero; else BLAKE3’s keyed hash under the first 32 bytes, zero-padded when there are fewer, with the bytes past them absorbed as the start of the input and one result() taken.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/hash/blake3.hpp>

blake3(
    void const* input_data,
    std::size_t input_size) noexcept;

Description

That result() only moves the output’s position, which the next update() starts again: a seed of 32 bytes K and more bytes R, then the input M, hashes as the seed K then the input R and M; with no update() after such a seed, the first result() returns bytes 32 to 63 of the output of K over R, the next 64 to 95, and so on. Two seeds of at most 32 bytes that differ only by trailing zero bytes are the same key.

Parameters

Name Description

input_data

The seed.

input_size

Its size.

webcpp::hash::digest_options

The parameters of a digest (spec 2.15), defined in digest.hpp; declared here for the engines, which take them.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/hash/digest.hpp>

template<class Digest>
struct digest_options;

Specializations

Name Description

digest_options<digests::blake2b>

BLAKE2b’s parameters (RFC 7693, section 2.5): a key, a salt, a personalisation and the output’s size, each part of the parameter block that starts the hash, so that each gives another function.

digest_options<digests::cshake_128>

cSHAKE128’s parameters (NIST SP 800-185, section 3): the function name N, which NIST reserves for functions it defines on cSHAKE, and the customisation string S, which an application chooses to separate its uses of the function from any other’s. With both empty, cSHAKE128 is SHAKE128.

digest_options<digests::cshake_256>

cSHAKE256’s parameters, as cSHAKE128’s (digest_options<digests::cshake_128>).

digest_options<digests::kt128>

KT128’s parameter (RFC 9861, section 3): the customisation string C, which an application chooses to separate its uses of the function from any other’s; empty by default. KT128 is a tree over TurboSHAKE128 that hashes a long input in chunks of 8,192 bytes, which an implementation may hash in parallel; its output is any size from 1 byte, the shorter the start of the longer.

digest_options<digests::kt256>

KT256’s parameter, as KT128’s (digest_options<digests::kt128>), over TurboSHAKE256.

digest_options<digests::parallelhash_128>

ParallelHash128’s parameters (NIST SP 800-185, section 6): the block size B in bytes, the customisation string S and the form, fixed-length or extendable-output (ParallelHashXOF128). ParallelHash cuts its input in blocks of B bytes, hashes each on its own (in parallel where an implementation can) and hashes the results: B is part of the function, and the same input under another B gives another digest.

digest_options<digests::parallelhash_256>

ParallelHash256’s parameters, as ParallelHash128’s (digest_options<digests::parallelhash_128>).

digest_options<digests::tuplehash_128>

TupleHash128’s parameters (NIST SP 800-185, section 5): the customisation string S and the form, fixed-length or extendable-output (TupleHashXOF128). TupleHash hashes a tuple of byte strings so that their bounds count: ("ab", "c") and ("a", "bc") give different digests. hasher::update takes one element of the tuple per call; digest_of hashes the tuple of one element, its input.

digest_options<digests::tuplehash_256>

TupleHash256’s parameters, as TupleHash128’s (digest_options<digests::tuplehash_128>).

digest_options<digests::turboshake_128>

TurboSHAKE’s parameter (RFC 9861, section 2.1): the domain separation byte D, which the sponge absorbs after the message, so that each value gives another function. The standard value is 0x1F; a protocol that builds several functions over TurboSHAKE gives each its own byte.

digest_options<digests::turboshake_256>

TurboSHAKE256’s parameter, as TurboSHAKE128’s (RFC 9861, section 2.1).

Template Parameters

Name Description

Digest

A tag of digests.

webcpp::hash::digest_options<digests::blake2b>

BLAKE2b’s parameters (RFC 7693, section 2.5): a key, a salt, a personalisation and the output’s size, each part of the parameter block that starts the hash, so that each gives another function.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/hash/digest.hpp>

template<>
struct digest_options<digests::blake2b>;

Description

std::array<std::uint8_t, 32> id{};
auto done = webcpp::hash::digest_of<webcpp::hash::digests::blake2b>(
    id, message, {.personalisation = app_tag, .output_size = 32});

The output’s size is an option, not the output span’s alone: BLAKE2b-256 is not BLAKE2b-512 cut to 32 bytes, and a hasher must know it when it starts. digest_of and hasher::finish take an output of exactly output_size bytes (invalid_output_size otherwise).

The spans are read during the call (digest_of, hasher::make) and not kept.

Data Members

Name Description

key

The key, 0 to 64 bytes (invalid_key_size past 64); empty, BLAKE2b unkeyed.

output_size

The output’s size, 1 to 64 bytes (invalid_output_size otherwise); 64 by default.

personalisation

The personalisation, a string that separates one application’s hashes from another’s: empty, or 16 bytes (invalid_parameters otherwise); a shorter tag is padded with zeros by the caller.

salt

The salt: empty, or 16 bytes (invalid_salt_size otherwise).

webcpp::hash::digest_options<digests::kt128>

KT128’s parameter (RFC 9861, section 3): the customisation string C, which an application chooses to separate its uses of the function from any other’s; empty by default. KT128 is a tree over TurboSHAKE128 that hashes a long input in chunks of 8,192 bytes, which an implementation may hash in parallel; its output is any size from 1 byte, the shorter the start of the longer.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/hash/digest.hpp>

template<>
struct digest_options<digests::kt128>;

Description

std::array<std::uint8_t, 32> digest{};
auto done = webcpp::hash::digest_of<webcpp::hash::digests::kt128>(
    digest, file_bytes, {.customisation = app_name});

KangarooTwelve absorbs C after the message, so hasher keeps the span make took and reads C at finish, not before: the caller keeps those bytes alive and unchanged until then (no copy, so no allocation). digest_of reads C during the call. On backends::xkcp where a size_t has 32 bits (wasm32), the message and C together are at most a little under 32 TiB (input_too_long, a refusal after which a hasher is spent), since XKCP counts the chunks in a size_t.

Data Members

customisation

The customisation string C, read at finish by a hasher.

webcpp::hash::digest_options<digests::parallelhash_128>

ParallelHash128’s parameters (NIST SP 800-185, section 6): the block size B in bytes, the customisation string S and the form, fixed-length or extendable-output (ParallelHashXOF128). ParallelHash cuts its input in blocks of B bytes, hashes each on its own (in parallel where an implementation can) and hashes the results: B is part of the function, and the same input under another B gives another digest.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/hash/digest.hpp>

template<>
struct digest_options<digests::parallelhash_128>;

Description

std::array<std::uint8_t, 32> digest{};
auto done = webcpp::hash::digest_of<webcpp::hash::digests::parallelhash_128>(
    digest, file_bytes, {.block_size = 8192});

SP 800-185 sets no default B: the call states it, and 0 is invalid_parameters. A backend may take fewer: XKCP takes a power of two of at least 8 bytes, and answers any other with unsupported_by_backend. The whole input, in one call or across a hasher’s updates, is at most SIZE_MAX / 8 bytes (input_too_long), since its length is counted in bits. The fixed-length form encodes the output’s length, as TupleHash’s does (digest_options<digests::tuplehash_128>), and is at most SIZE_MAX / 8 bytes (invalid_output_size), as is S (input_too_long), which is read during the call and not kept.

xof

The extendable-output form, ParallelHashXOF128, in place of the fixed-length one.

webcpp::hash::digest_options<digests::tuplehash_128>

TupleHash128’s parameters (NIST SP 800-185, section 5): the customisation string S and the form, fixed-length or extendable-output (TupleHashXOF128). TupleHash hashes a tuple of byte strings so that their bounds count: ("ab", "c") and ("a", "bc") give different digests. hasher::update takes one element of the tuple per call; digest_of hashes the tuple of one element, its input.

The fixed-length form encodes the output’s length L, so that its digests of 32 and 64 bytes are unrelated; the XOF form encodes none, and its shorter output is the start of its longer. webcpp::hash::hasher

A hash fed in pieces, with one result: make, update as often as the data comes, then finish once (spec 2.15).

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/hash/digest.hpp>

template<
    class Digest,
    class Backend = default_backend<Digest>>
class hasher;

Description

Unlike Boost.Hash2’s types, the result is final: an update or a finish after finish, or on a hasher moved from, is error::invalid_state.

Move-only. The state is wiped (and what the backend allocated for it freed) by finish, by the destructor, and in the hasher moved from.

auto hashing = webcpp::hash::hasher<webcpp::hash::digests::sha2_256>::make();
if (!hashing) {
    return hashing.error();
}
for (auto piece : pieces) {
    if (auto fed = hashing->update(piece); !fed) {
        return fed.error();
    }
}
std::array<std::uint8_t, 32> id{};
auto done = hashing->finish(id);

webcpp::hash::async_argon2id

Argon2id (RFC 9106, one lane) on a thread of work’s context (spec 11.5).

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/hash/async.hpp>

template<
    class Backend = default_backend<kdfs::argon2id>,
    class WorkExecutor,
    class CompletionToken>
auto
async_argon2id(
    WorkExecutor const& work,
    std::span<uint8_t> output,
    std::span<uint8_t const> password,
    std::span<uint8_t const> salt,
    argon2id_parameters const& parameters,
    CompletionToken&& token);

Description

The guards of argon2id first, whose refusal completes through a post; then the work, posted to work (a webcpp::asio::thread_pool’s executor, typically); the completion on the handler’s associated executor (work by default; a program binds its event loop’s with bind_executor), so that the event loop never blocks. Exists only where the build has threads (WEBCPP_HASH_HAS_THREADS).

Cancellation through the handler’s slot: before the work starts, any type completes the operation at once with operation_aborted, the work never runs; during it, a terminal or partial one lets the work end (libsodium cannot be interrupted), then output is zeroed and the completion is operation_aborted (a total one is then ignored: zeroing is a side effect). "At once" is on the handler’s associated executor: for a handler without one, that is work, so the completion waits for its threads; bind the handler to the event loop’s executor, and emit the signal there too, never from another thread, as Asio’s slots require.

Return Value

What the completion token’s async_result gives. The completion’s code is empty on success, or argon2id’s error, or operation_aborted.

webcpp::hash::async_pbkdf2

PBKDF2 (RFC 8018), asynchronously.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/hash/async.hpp>

template<
    class Hmac,
    class Backend = default_async_backend<kdfs::pbkdf2, Hmac>,
    class Executor,
    class CompletionToken>
auto
async_pbkdf2(
    Executor const& executor,
    std::span<uint8_t> output,
    std::span<uint8_t const> password,
    std::span<uint8_t const> salt,
    uint64_t iterations,
    CompletionToken&& token);

Description

On a synchronous backend, the default, a heavy function (spec 11.5): the work runs on a thread of executor’s context (a webcpp::asio::thread_pool’s) and completes on the handler’s associated executor (executor by default; a program binds its event loop’s with bind_executor), and it exists only where the build has threads (WEBCPP_HASH_HAS_THREADS). On backends::webcrypto, on Emscripten, the browser runs it and no thread is needed: there executor must be that of an io_context run on the calling thread, whose run returns to the JavaScript event loop where WebCrypto’s promise settles (ruling R73). The context is checked: a concrete executor of another context (a thread_pool’s) stops the build, and a type-erased one (any_io_executor) whose context is not an io_context, or whose io_context executor it hides behind another allocator or two concrete strands, completes with invalid_parameters, posted to the handler’s associated executor. The calling thread is the program’s duty, not checked. WebCrypto takes at most 2^32 - 1 iterations (invalid_iterations) and an output of at most (2^32 - 1) / 8 bytes (invalid_output_size), over hmac_sha1_160, hmac_sha2_256, hmac_sha2_384 and hmac_sha2_512 alone.

Cancellation through the handler’s slot, on a synchronous backend: before the work starts, any type completes the operation at once with operation_aborted, the work never runs; during it, a terminal or partial one lets the work end, then output is zeroed and the completion is operation_aborted (a total one is then ignored). "At once" is on the handler’s associated executor: for a handler without one, that is executor, so the completion waits for its threads; bind the handler to the event loop’s executor, and emit the signal there too, never from another thread, as Asio’s slots require. On backends::webcrypto a terminal or partial one completes at once with operation_aborted, output zeroed, while the browser’s work runs to its end unseen; a total one is ignored.

Return Value

What the completion token’s async_result gives. The completion’s code is empty on success, or pbkdf2’s error, a guard’s refusal completing through a post, output untouched; or operation_aborted. On backends::webcrypto also invalid_parameters (the executor), output untouched, and backend_failure (a rejected promise, an unexpected result, no WebCrypto), output zeroed.

The pseudorandom function, as hmac_sha2_512.

An Asio executor: of the threads the work runs on, or WebCrypto’s io_context’s.

CompletionToken

An Asio completion token of signature void(boost::system::error_code).

The work executor, or WebCrypto’s io_context executor.

webcpp::hash::kbkdf

SP 800-108’s key-based key derivation (NIST SP 800-108r1, section 4.1, counter mode) over the HMAC Hmac: fills output from the key-derivation key key, each block an HMAC under key of the counter, then the fixed input options states.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/hash/kdf_standards.hpp>

    class Hmac,
    class Backend = default_backend<kdfs::kbkdf_hmac, Hmac>>
[[nodiscard]]
boost::system::result<void>
kbkdf(
    std::span<uint8_t> output,
    std::span<uint8_t const> key,
    kbkdf_options const& options = {});

Description

std::array<std::uint8_t, 32> derived{};
auto done = webcpp::hash::kbkdf<webcpp::hash::hmac_sha2_256, webcpp::hash::backends::openssl>(
    derived, key, {.label = label, .context = context});

Return Value

Success; or the first guard’s error (invalid_parameters for a counter width other than 8, 16, 24 or 32, invalid_output_size, invalid_key_size, unsupported_by_backend), output untouched; or errc::not_enough_memory or backend_failure, output zeroed.

Note

The return value should not be discarded.

Template Parameters

Name Description

Hmac

The PRF, a Boost.Hash2 hmac, as hmac_sha2_256. SP 800-108r1 approves HMAC over an approved hash function (SHA-1, SHA-2, SHA-3); unlike sskdf and x963kdf, which refuse a digest their standard does not take, kbkdf takes every hmac its backend has, MD5’s, RIPEMD-160’s and BLAKE2’s included, for the protocols outside NIST’s approval that use them. Where approval matters, take HMAC over SHA-2 or SHA-3.

Backend

The backend; by default default_backend of kdfs::kbkdf_hmac, which has none (design D34): the call names backends::openssl, which has every hmac of hmac.hpp but hmac_ripemd_128.

Parameters

Name Description

output

K_OUT, its size the length L: 1 byte up to (2^r - 1) digests, and, when options.length, at most 536,870,911 bytes (L in bits fits its 32 bits). It must not overlap the inputs.

key

K_IN, the key-derivation key: at least 1 byte (backends::openssl: at most INT_MAX, HMAC’s key length in OpenSSL, unsupported_by_backend beyond).

options

The label, the context, the counter’s width and which parts the fixed input holds.

WEBCPP_HASH_HAS_THREADS

Defined where the heavy functions of <webcpp/hash/async.hpp> (async_argon2id, async_argon2, async_scrypt, async_pbkdf2 on a synchronous backend) run on another thread: natively, where Boost.Config’s BOOST_HAS_THREADS is defined (every native build, b2’s threading=single included), and on Emscripten built with -pthread (b2’s threading=multi); never on wasip2 or wasip3, whose cooperative threads do not run in parallel. Without it each of those names refuses at compile time.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/hash/config.hpp>

#define WEBCPP_HASH_HAS_THREADS

See Also

"Asynchronous calls", in the guide.

WEBCPP_HASH_NO_EXCEPTIONS

Defined when webcpp::hash is built without exceptions: when webcpp has none (the compiler has none, or the developer defined WEBCPP_NO_EXCEPTIONS for every webcpp library), or when the developer defines it alone.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/hash/config.hpp>

#define WEBCPP_HASH_NO_EXCEPTIONS

Description

webcpp::hash raises no exception of its own: every operation that can fail reports it as a value, whether or not the macro is defined.

See Also

"Exceptions", in the guide.

WEBCPP_HASH_NO_THREADS

Defined by the developer to leave WEBCPP_HASH_HAS_THREADS undefined in a build that has threads: the heavy functions of <webcpp/hash/async.hpp> then refuse at compile time, so that no call of the program can start a thread’s work.

Synopsis

Declared in <webcpp/hash/config.hpp>

Appendix A: Changelog

What changed in hash in each version of webcpp, newest first, one line per change. "Unreleased" is what the next version brings. The release notes of every version are on webcpp’s index page.

Unreleased

  • Added the library: Boost.Hash2’s algorithms and HMAC under webcpp::hash’s names, keccak_256 (Ethereum’s Keccak-256 over XKCP), blake3 (keyed, key derivation, extendable output), every result [[nodiscard]].

  • Added HKDF (RFC 5869) and PBKDF2 (RFC 8018) over Boost.Hash2’s hmacs on hash2; argon2id (RFC 9106) with libsodium’s presets, scrypt (RFC 7914) and argon2’s Argon2i and Argon2id on sodium.

  • Added backends::openssl, OpenSSL 3.5.9 through /webcpp/hash//openssl (native, wasip2, wasip3), named in the call: HKDF, PBKDF2, scrypt, every Argon2 parameter, KBKDF, SSKDF, X9.63 KDF, its digests and MACs.

  • Added backends::sodium’s HKDF over HMAC-SHA-256/512, BLAKE2b with key, salt, personalisation and length, keyed BLAKE2b (macs::blake2b_mac), SipHash-2-4, SipHash-2-4x, blake2b_subkey, SHA-256/512, SHA3-256/512, SHAKE, TurboSHAKE with its domain byte, and HMAC-SHA-256/512.

  • Added backends::bearssl’s HKDF over MD5, SHA-1 and SHA-2 (hkdf alone), and its MD5, SHA-1, SHA-2, MD5-SHA1, SHAKE and HMAC as digests and MACs, named in the call.

  • Added the default backend of every function and tag, the first of hash2, xkcp, blake3 and sodium that has it, and doc/capabilities.json naming each default and backends::webcrypto’s asynchronous-only cells.

  • Added async.hpp, async_digest, async_hmac, async_hkdf, async_pbkdf2, async_argon2id, async_argon2 and async_scrypt over webcpp::asio, and backends::webcrypto, the browser’s WebCrypto, for them on Emscripten.

  • Added the measured tables (doc/measurements.*) from release builds, a reference of 2026-11-16 that decides nothing, and allocation tests: none in hash’s code.

  • Added the guide: chapters per family and per use case, an example per section, generated tables and llms.txt, and a Boost.Hash2 proposal of keccak_224 to keccak_512.

  • Added the families digest_of, hasher, mac and argon2 over digests, macs and kdfs tags on hash2, xkcp (Keccak, SHA-3, SHAKE, SP 800-185, KangarooTwelve, TurboSHAKE), blake3 and sodium, and error::invalid_state.
